headline: Sensex surges over 1,500 points as foreign fund inflows and lower crude oil trigger massive market rally

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Strong foreign institutional investor (FII) buying and fund inflows
Decline in global crude oil prices
Rally in FMCG and private banking stocks leading sector gains
Positive market momentum from reverse AI trade sentiment
whatHappening: Sensex surged over 1,500 to 2,000 points, while Nifty 50 reclaimed the 25,800 mark and reached intraday highs of 25,951
Indian equities rallied 1.8%, helping recoup nearly all losses recorded in 2026 during November
Carlyle reduced its holding in Piramal Pharma by selling a 7.4% stake for over Rs 2,211 crore
US markets faced severe selling pressure with Nasdaq plunging 4% amid renewed AI sector concerns
summary:
Indian stock markets surged significantly on November 25, with the Sensex jumping over 1,500 points and Nifty 50 reclaiming the 25,800 level.
The rally was fueled by robust foreign fund inflows, lower crude oil prices, and strong buying in private banking and FMCG sectors.
The November gains have enabled Indian benchmark indices to recover nearly all losses suffered earlier in 2026.
